articles.title: GPT-6.1 Terra with Microsoft Agent Framework: A PDF Invoice Agent in C#
articles.excerpt: GPT-6.1 Terra with Microsoft Agent Framework: A PDF Invoice Agent in C In the GPT-6.1 Terra post, I built an invoice agent with nothing but HttpClient. It reads a PDF invoice, calls a C# function to c…
articles.body: GPT-6.1 Terra with Microsoft Agent Framework: A PDF Invoice Agent in C In the GPT-6.1 Terra post , I built an invoice agent with nothing but HttpClient . It reads a PDF invoice, calls a C# function to check the supplier, and returns a structured result that lands in a C# record. Doing it by hand meant writing the JSON, the tool loop, the response chaining and the schema myself. That was the point: you could see every byte that goes to the Responses API. This post builds the same agent with Microsoft Agent Framework. Same model, same PDF, same tool, same record. The framework writes the JSON, runs the tool loop and builds the schema, so the sample drops from about 320 lines to 136. It isn't free, though.

articles.title: Don't turn the moon into the Wild West, scientists warn
articles.excerpt: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing the lunar environment may suffer irreversible damage if things move too fast.
articles.body: Researchers are calling for a moratorium on industrial exploitation of the moon, fearing that rapid development could cause irreversible environmental damage and destroy invaluable scientific material. Both China and the U.S. are pushing forward with plans to establish permanent human settlements on the moon by the end of the next decade. Commercial players want to build businesses supporting these future explorers by mining for resources such as water , construction materials, industrial metals and rare earth minerals. However, some scientists argue that a temporary ban on lunar industrialization is necessary to allow regulations to catch up and limit what can be allowed in order to prevent a moon rush from destroying the pristine lunar environment.
articles.author: Tereza Pultarova

articles.title: A leaky AI supply chain is exposing secret user data at an alarming rate
articles.excerpt: Test using prompts with unique, trackable secrets proves that data doesn't stay private.
articles.body: Researchers planted 2 million digital tripwires in requests sent through a sprawling network of AI services to find out what happened to sensitive information entrusted to them. What they discovered was an ecosystem that leaked highly sensitive data like a sieve. The exposure was found through an ingenious experiment designed to test if sensitive information can leak through the vast chain of widely used AI services and how that information is exploited when it does. Many of today’s AI apps use services such as OpenRouter or Vercel that act as brokers.

Why Physical AI Evaluation is Different Evaluating Physical AI is fundamentally different from evaluating conventional digital artificial intelligence because intelligent decisions must produce reliable outcomes in the physical world. articles.excerpt: STATERA Library · Series 09 · Volume 11 · Chapter 01 · EN https://github.com/Statera-Library/09_Vol_11_Physical_AI_Evaluation_and_Benchmarking/blob/main/Chapter_01_Evaluation_Philosophy_for_Physical_A…
articles.body: STATERA Library · Series 09 · Volume 11 · Chapter 01 · EN Source: https://github.com/Statera-Library/09_Vol_11_Physical_AI_Evaluation_and_Benchmarking/blob/main/Chapter_01_Evaluation_Philosophy_for_Physical_AI/Chapter_01_Evaluation_Philosophy_for_Physical_AI_EN.md Volume 11. Physical AI Evaluation and Benchmarking Chapter 01. Evaluation Philosophy for Physical AI 01.01. What Should Physical AI Evaluation Measure Physical AI evaluation should measure how effectively an intelligent system perceives, reasons about, acts upon, and adapts to the physical world. Unlike conventional artificial intelligence, which can often be assessed through prediction accuracy or benchmark scores, Physical AI must demonstrate meaningful behavior under real physical constraints.

articles.excerpt: STATERA Library · Series 09 · Volume 11 · Chapter 02 · EN https://github.com/Statera-Library/09_Vol_11_Physical_AI_Evaluation_and_Benchmarking/blob/main/Chapter_02_Simulation_Benchmarks/Chapter_02_Sim…

Physical AI Evaluation and Benchmarking Chapter 02. Simulation Benchmarks 02.01. Why Benchmark in Simulation Simulation benchmarking provides a controlled and repeatable foundation for evaluating Physical AI systems before deployment in real environments. Unlike conventional software, Physical AI interacts with objects, surfaces, sensors, actuators, and dynamic surroundings.

articles.title: Physical AI Evaluation and Benchmarking — Ch.03: Real World Benchmarks [EN]

Physical AI Evaluation and Benchmarking Chapter 03. Real World Benchmarks 03.01. Why Real World Benchmarking is Essential Real-world benchmarking is essential because Physical AI systems must demonstrate reliable performance in environments governed by actual physical constraints rather than idealized computational assumptions. Although simulation provides efficient and repeatable experimentation, it cannot reproduce every interaction among sensors, actuators, materials, humans, and environmental conditions.

articles.title: There's an impostor hiding in the Hyades star cluster. Can you spot it?
articles.excerpt: Aldebaran looks for all the world like the brightest member of the Hyades star cluster. It isn't — and discovering why changes the way you look at constellations.
articles.body: For years I looked at Taurus and saw something perfectly sensible. There was the Hyades, the big V-shaped cluster that forms the bull's face, with Aldebaran, noticeably brighter and more orange than the other stars, the dominant star. Every diagram reinforced the arrangement — Aldebaran was the eye of Taurus, the Hyades made the face, and in my head they became one object. Then I discovered that Aldebaran has nothing to do with the Hyades. I remember going outside afterward and looking again, half expecting the deception to become obvious now that I knew. It didn't. Aldebaran still looked completely at home among the other stars . The difference is hidden in the one dimension our eyes judge poorly when we look into space — depth.
articles.author: Jamie Carter

articles.title: Could an ancient solar eclipse rewrite Egyptian history?
articles.excerpt: A biblical mystery, an ancient Egyptian inscription and a "ring of fire" solar eclipse 3,200 years ago hold clues to when Ramesses the Great ruled.
articles.body: The solar system is a clock that can be run in both directions. On Aug. 2, 2027, that clock will bring the moon's dark central shadow — a path of totality — back to Egypt. A t otal solar eclipse will sweep across the country , passing directly over Luxor and plunging some of ancient Egypt's greatest surviving monuments into darkness. Totality will begin in Luxor at approximately 1:02 p.m. EEST and last 6 minutes 22 seconds, according to Time and Date . We know when it will happen because we can calculate the motions of Earth and the moon centuries in advance. But run the same celestial clock backward and eclipses become one of nature's most precise timestamps. Astronomers can reconstruct where the moon's shadow fell thousands of years ago, even when nobody left a record of it.
